riskFactors.label: Adult smoking rate
riskFactors.derivation: OHID smoking-attributable admissions 2022/23 (412,171, ages 35+) divided by all hospital admissions aged 35+ (HES 2023/24, 13,713,682) gives an attributable fraction of 3.0%. With adult smoking prevalence 11.5% (2022) this implies a relative risk of 1.27.
riskFactors.note: OHID's attributable count includes harm in ex-smokers, so the effect of quitting builds up over many years.

riskFactors.label: Adult obesity rate
riskFactors.derivationPublished: Million Women Study (Reeves et al. 2014): admission rates per woman over 10 years of 3.0 (BMI 30-35) and 3.5 (35+) versus 2.4-2.6 below BMI 30, giving a relative risk of 1.28 for obesity.
riskFactors.derivation: Between-area regression of age-standardised emergency admissions (OHID 93227) on adult obesity prevalence, adjusted for deprivation and smoking, across 147 local authorities: +1.07% admissions per percentage point (95% CI +0.57 to +1.57). Equivalent relative risk 2.49.
riskFactors.note: An association between areas, not a proven causal effect; see the Validation page.

riskFactors.label: Alcohol harm
riskFactors.derivation: OHID alcohol-related admissions, narrow measure, 2023/24: 280,747, 1.6% of all admissions (HES 2023/24).
riskFactors.help: Change in admissions caused by alcohol (e.g. from minimum unit pricing or treatment services).

deprivation.note: Age-standardised emergency admission ratio (OHID 93227, 2018-based pooled period) for 151 upper-tier local authorities grouped into fifths by IMD 2019 deprivation score (most deprived first), relative to the average. Area-level, so it understates the gap between individuals.
deprivation.help: Narrow the gap in emergency admission rates between the most and least deprived fifths of areas.

veSource.name: Bucholc et al. 2026, Influenza Other Respir Viruses (Northern Ireland 2024/25, aged 65+)

flu.note: Vaccine effectiveness cannot be estimated from area-level data (placebo outcomes fail; see Validation), so the measured estimate from a UK test-negative study is used.
